From 9aab1c3d7299285e2569cbc0ed5892d631a241b2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Guangshuo Li <lgs201920130244@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 17:53:27 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] ice: fix double free in ice_sf_eth_activate() error path

When auxiliary_device_add() fails, ice_sf_eth_activate() jumps to
aux_dev_uninit and calls auxiliary_device_uninit(&sf_dev->adev).

The device release callback ice_sf_dev_release() frees sf_dev, but
the current error path falls through to sf_dev_free and calls
kfree(sf_dev) again, causing a double free.

Keep kfree(sf_dev) for the auxiliary_device_init() failure path, but
avoid falling through to sf_dev_free after auxiliary_device_uninit().

Fixes: 13acc5c4cdbe ("ice: subfunction activation and base devlink ops")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Aleksandr Loktionov <aleksandr.loktionov@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Guangshuo Li <lgs201920130244@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Jacob Keller <jacob.e.keller@intel.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260416-iwl-net-submission-2026-04-14-v2-3-686c33c9828d@intel.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_sf_eth.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_sf_eth.c
index 2cf04bc6edce..a730aa368c92 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_sf_eth.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_sf_eth.c
@@ -305,6 +305,8 @@ ice_sf_eth_activate(struct ice_dynamic_port *dyn_port,
 
 aux_dev_uninit:
 	auxiliary_device_uninit(&sf_dev->adev);
+	return err;
+
 sf_dev_free:
 	kfree(sf_dev);
 xa_erase:
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### Files Modified
- **`drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_sf_eth.c`**

### Modifications in the File
In the function `ice_sf_eth_activate`, the error handling path was corrected by inserting a `return err;` statement after the `auxiliary_device_uninit(&sf_dev->adev)` call. This change prevents the code from falling through to the `sf_dev_free:` label, which would have called `kfree(sf_dev)` a second time.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- **Single file, single logical change**: The fix only affects the error path inside `ice_sf_eth_activate`.  
- **Before the patch**: When `auxiliary_device_add()` failed, the code jumped to `aux_dev_uninit`, called `auxiliary_device_uninit()` (which triggers `ice_sf_dev_release()` and frees `sf_dev`), then fell through to `sf_dev_free` and called `kfree(sf_dev)` again – causing a double-free bug.  
- **After the patch**: The `return err;` statement immediately exits the function after `auxiliary_device_uninit()`, so the subsequent `kfree(sf_dev)` is never reached. The `sf_dev_free:` label is still used for the earlier failure path (`auxiliary_device_init()` failure), where `kfree(sf_dev)` remains necessary because the release callback has not been set up yet.

This minimal change eliminates the double free without altering other parts of the error handling logic.

Root cause:
In ice_sf_eth_activate(), when auxiliary_device_add() fails, the error handling path calls auxiliary_device_uninit() which triggers ice_sf_dev_release() to free sf_dev, but then falls through to sf_dev_free label which calls kfree(sf_dev) again, causing a double free. The fix adds a return statement after auxiliary_device_uninit() to prevent the fall-through.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
aux_dev_uninit:
    auxiliary_device_uninit(&sf_dev->adev);
sf_dev_free:
    kfree(sf_dev);
Reason:
After `auxiliary_device_uninit()` triggers the release callback `ice_sf_dev_release()` which frees `sf_dev`, the execution falls through to the `sf_dev_free` label, where `kfree(sf_dev)` is called again, resulting in a double free.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
aux_dev_uninit:
    auxiliary_device_uninit(&sf_dev->adev);
    return err;
sf_dev_free:
    kfree(sf_dev);
Reason:
Adding a `return err` statement after `auxiliary_device_uninit()` prevents the fall-through to `sf_dev_free`, thus avoiding the double free. The `kfree(sf_dev)` at `sf_dev_free` is still needed for the `auxiliary_device_init()` failure path, where `sf_dev` has not been freed by the release callback.
